sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Microfluidic Cartridges and Immunoassay Analyzers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Common Law corporate statutory framework with indigenous customary law in limited land and traditional matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America, Title II economic provisions (1986; Amended Compact entered into force 1 May 2004)
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA), regional free trade agreement under the Pacific Islands Forum
No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty with the United States or the European Union currently in force
No comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) in force with the United States or major OECD jurisdictions; tax exemption relies on the RMI non-resident offshore corporate regime

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) AML/CFT regime is principally governed by the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000 (as amended) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Regulations 2012, together with FIU Directives issued by the Ministry of Finance. Corporate and registered-agent duties are codified in the Business Corporations Act 2002 (sections 100–112) and the Registered Agents Regulations. The RMI Financial Intelligence Unit exercises supervisory oversight under the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering framework and UN Security Council Resolution obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the RMI Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of execution or licensed RMI notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the executing jurisdiction is a Contracting State) OR Consular Legalization at the nearest RMI Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport and proof of residential address for each proposed director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the document-origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the nearest RMI Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration / Certificate of Beneficial Ownership executed by the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the executing jurisdiction or the RMI Registered Agent's AML Compliance Officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the nearest RMI Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate extract for any corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing registry is in a Contracting State) OR Consular Legalization at the nearest RMI Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized signature pages of the Articles of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator or authorized officer before a Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at the nearest RMI Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watchlist, the United States OFAC SDN List, the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, and the United Kingdom HM Treasury sanctions list. Foreign PEP status is determined under FATF definitions and triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Adverse screening results require a Suspicious Transaction Report to the RMI FIU and prohibit incorporation unless the relevant authority grants an exemption. Screening records must be retained in the registered agent's AML/CFT compliance file for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands – name availability is confirmed through licensed registered agents; there is no public self-service online search portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in Latin/Roman characters; English is the working language of the RMI corporate registry. A name in a non-Roman script must be transliterated into a Romanized English form. The legal name must include a permissible corporate designator, such as Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, Corp., Inc., or Ltd. The name must be distinguishable on the register and may not be misleading as to the entity type or regulated status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice. Within 14 calendar days, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, setting out the distinguishing features of the proposed name and any supporting evidence. The appeal fee is US$100. The Registrar must issue a written ruling within 15 business days. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the appeal is granted only upon production of a no-objection letter or license from the relevant sector regulator. A further judicial remedy is available by originating motion in the RMI High Court. A name reservation may be extended for additional 90-day periods by filing a renewal application and paying the prescribed fee before the original window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for statutory corporate purposes; the registered agent's official RMI address may serve as the registered office. For the stated IVD equipment manufacturing scope, no physical operational office inside the Marshall Islands is required for a non-resident Business Corporation. However, a virtual office does not establish economic substance for foreign tax or regulatory licensing purposes, and most commercial banks will reject a virtual-only address for account opening. A substantive operational address in the manufacturing jurisdiction and appropriate ISO/FDA/CE licensing documentation are required for banking and commercial counterparty due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 2% annualized probability for a non-resident manufacturing Business Corporation with no physical RMI operations or assets; the likelihood rises to approximately 35% if the registered agent's file is selected by the RMI FIU for AML/CFT compliance inspection or if the entity applies for an RMI banking, trust, or insurance license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the RMI Corporate Registry Fee Schedule (Business Corporations Act, section 13)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee (authorized capital up to US$50,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory incorporation fee under the Business Corporations Act Fee Schedule, Part 1

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Agent service fee – first year appointment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a single non-resident Business Corporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO file preparation, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional benchmark for enhanced due diligence under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000 and APG guidance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille and/or RMI consular legalization bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public in the origin jurisdiction and, where required, the nearest RMI Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per notarial/consular fee schedule for a standard corporate KYC document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Optional statutory expedited fee where the Registrar offers 24-hour priority processing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, Title 51 of the Marshall Islands Revised Statutes, as amended (Sections 9, 13, 18, 24, 26, 52, 73 and 107); Foreign Investment Business License Act 1999 (conditional); Environmental Protection Act 1984 (conditional)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro; filings are lodged through a licensed RMI Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) submitted under Section 9 of the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares must have par value and the Board fixes initial paid-up capital (e.g., USD 1,000 for 1,000 common shares of USD 1.00 par value); no escrow account, notarized capital commitment, or inward capital deposit requirement; annual franchise fee on authorized capital applies (minimum USD 100)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws be, and hereby are, approved and adopted; the Board is authorized to issue the subscribed common shares for lawful consideration as determined by the Board, no statutory escrow being required. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the registered agent named in the Articles be, and hereby are, adopted and maintained in good standing by the Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are elected officers until the first annual meeting: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; any two officers acting together are authorized to open and operate bank accounts, execute banking documents, and effect all registrations, licenses, and filings for the Corporation's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Reservation of Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro (via licensed RMI Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application listing three proposed corporate names in order of priority; each name must end with 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or an approved abbreviation; the authorized agent verifies availability and reserves the name for 30 calendar days; reserving the name does not confer incorporation rights.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (Form NR-1)
Consent letter from the proposed RMI registered agent
Identification of the authorized corporate registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first-choice name is rejected for conflict or prohibited wording, the Registrar automatically reviews the second and third alternatives; the applicant must submit an acceptable alternate name or a written consent from the existing name holder within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed RMI corporate attorney and notary public acting for the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws in conformity with the Business Corporations Act; the Articles must state the corporate name, registered office address in Majuro, name of the registered agent, authorized share structure, par value, business purpose (manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers), and the election of non-resident domestic corporation status; the sole incorporator executes the Articles before a notary; initial Bylaws may be adopted by the incorporator or deferred to the first Board.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1)
Bylaws of the Corporation
Appointment and consent of RMI registered agent
Incorporator subscription statement for initial shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If drafting counsel identifies a legal defect or omission, a corrected instrument is re-executed and re-notarized before filing; no Registry remedy applies at this stage because submission has not yet occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent lodges the notarized Articles of Incorporation together with the government filing fee of USD 170; the Registrar examines the instrument for statutory compliance; upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the corporation comes into existence on the effective date stated therein.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1)
Government filing fee receipt
Registered agent consent and undertaking
Certificate of incorporation application cover sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a notice of non-compliance, the applicant has 15 calendar days under Section 18 to file corrected Articles; if the defect relates to the registered agent, substitute an eligible agent and resubmit; a resubmission fee applies for re-examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations; licensed RMI registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office in Majuro is a physical street address distinct from a post-office box; ensure the registered agent has executed the statutory consent and is available to accept service of process; maintain registered office records, statutory registers, and share records at the registered office as required by the Act.
required_dossiers: Consent and acceptance of appointment of registered agent
Registered office address confirmation
Statutory corporate records and registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or becomes disqualified, the Board must appoint a successor agent and file the change with the Registrar within 30 days; failure results in administrative dissolution after 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Appointments and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the Board of Directors, which may be conducted by unanimous written consent; adopt or ratify the Bylaws, approve the issuance of initial shares to the subscriber, appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, and authorize the opening of bank accounts and execution of banking documentation; execute share certificates and enter them in the share register.
required_dossiers: Written consent or minutes of the first Board meeting
Officer appointment resolutions
Share subscription agreements and share certificates
Bank account opening resolution and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an act of the first Board is later found defective, the Board may ratify it by unanimous written consent; retroactive validation is permitted under the Act unless the defect violates a mandatory provision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Tax-Exempt Status Declaration and Annual Franchise Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations; Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporation's non-resident domestic status is declared in the Articles; request from the Registrar a certified confirmation of non-resident tax-exempt status under Section 107; pay the annual franchise fee based on authorized capital and file the annual corporate report; the exemption is self-executing and no separate income tax registration is required for non-resident corporations with no RMI-source business income.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Section 107 non-resident status declaration
Annual report and franchise fee payment schedule
Evidence of no RMI-source business operations (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the non-resident exemption is challenged, submit a statutory declaration and supporting evidence demonstrating no income derived from RMI sources; any local business activity requires alternative licensing under the Foreign Investment Business License Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conditional Foreign Investment Business License and Industrial Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign Investment Board, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; relevant sectoral regulators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: This step applies only if the non-resident corporation establishes a physical manufacturing, assembly, or service facility within Marshall Islands territory; in that case, file a Foreign Investment Business License application with the Foreign Investment Board before commencing operations; if manufacturing occurs outside the RMI and the corporation conducts only offshore commercial activity, no RMI industrial license or environmental permit is triggered; document the condition in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Business License application form
Business plan and investment particulars
Certificate of Incorporation and articles
Lease or site control evidence for any RMI facility
RMI EPA environmental registration, if physical operations commence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Foreign Investment Board denies or queries the application, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade within 30 days; the corporation may also restructure to operate exclusively through a separately licensed local entity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Foreign Investment Board, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; Marshal Islands Environmental Protection Authority; Majuro Fire and Life Safety Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) under the Foreign Investment Business License Act 1999; supplemental RMI EPA Facility Operating Permit for regulated manufacturing activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA), Office of the President
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Registration and Facility Operating Permit, with environmental screening trigger; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report becomes mandatory only if reagent storage exceeds 500 liters of volatile organic compounds per month, wastewater discharge exceeds 25 cubic meters per day, or the facility is located within 100 meters of protected marine or freshwater habitat
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: RMI EPA effluent and emission standards under the Environmental Protection Act 1984: pH 6.0-9.0; BOD5 not exceeding 25 mg/L; TSS not exceeding 30 mg/L; total residual chlorine not exceeding 0.05 mg/L; zero discharge to groundwater; volatile organic compound abatement efficiency of at least 85% with stack concentration not exceeding 20 mg/m3; hazardous immunoassay reagents stored in bunded secondary containment; cleanroom production areas maintained to ISO 14644 Class 7 standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Life Safety Certificate from the Majuro Fire and Life Safety Division in accordance with the Marshall Islands Fire Prevention Code and NFPA 101; structural load inspection and building clearance from the Ministry of Public Works for any industrial premises; occupational health and safety clearance under the RMI Occupational Health and Safety Regulations requiring mechanical ventilation and exhaust verification, hazardous materials storage inspection, emergency evacuation plan, and worker exposure monitoring for biological and chemical agents used in IVD manufacturing

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Revenue & Taxation Division (income/tax administration) and the RMI Customs Service (import duties) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands; Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA) for payroll contributions; Foreign Investment Board for the Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL). Portal: official RMI government web portal (no dedicated national e-tax filing system for tax-exempt non-resident corporations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Non-Resident Business Corporation (BC) is incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (BCA) 1990 (Delaware-modeled) through the Registrar of Corporations, receiving a Certificate of Incorporation; no national income-tax TIN or VAT ID is issued because the BC is statutorily exempt from RMI income tax. SOP: (1) file Articles of Incorporation (including non-resident status clauses) and appoint a local Registered Agent; (2) obtain the annual franchise fee receipt/good standing certificate from the Registrar; (3) if any physical operations or employment occur in the RMI, register with MISSA and obtain a FIBL; (4) for any imports/exports, obtain a Customs Importer/Exporter ID from the RMI Customs Service; the corporate registration certificate and Customs ID serve as the operative identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The RMI has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. A BC may elect, in its Articles of Incorporation, to be a 'Non-Resident Domestic Corporation' (0% RMI tax on foreign-source income and no territorial nexus), and shipping entities may elect Foreign Maritime Entity status. An entity that elects to carry on business in the RMI becomes liable to FIBL, MISSA, municipal wage tax (Majuro/Kwajalein) and customs duty; tax treatment follows incorporation status and in-country substance rather than elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or general sales tax; the RMI operates a customs import duty (tariff) system under the Customs Tariff Act 1997, plus municipal wage taxes and MISSA/health-fund payroll contributions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST turnover registration threshold exists. All commercial importers must register with the RMI Customs Service for an importer ID; any foreign-owned business operating in the RMI must obtain a FIBL; any employer with payroll must register with MISSA regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The RMI imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping mandate. Invoices are private commercial documents and are not pre-cleared by the Ministry of Finance; customs declarations are submitted through the RMI Customs Service using standard paper or electronic manifests, with no mandatory government API integration for export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Technically inapplicable as the RMI has no VAT/GST; there is no zero-rating claim to file. Exports of IVD microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers leave the RMI customs territory free of any RMI export tax, customs duty, or turnover tax, and a Non-Resident BC retains its 0% tax-exempt status provided (i) goods are physically exported, (ii) no RMI domestic sales are made, and (iii) the entity does not become resident by carrying on business in the RMI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward entry filed with the RMI Customs Service)
Commercial Invoice fully describing the IVD medical devices and values
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from the RMI
Packing List (carton-level details for customs verification)
Certificate of Origin (where required by the destination market)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing FX repatriation through SWIFT LC or TT Wire
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although there is no VAT output tax to claw back, fraudulent or unsupported export declarations are prosecuted under the Customs Tariff Act 1997 and the Business Corporations Act 1990. Penalties include monetary fines and penalties (plus interest), seizure and forfeiture of the exported goods, revocation of the FIBL or customs registration, deregistration of the non-resident BC, and criminal liability for directors. If the entity cannot substantiate physical export, non-resident status, or FX repatriation within the 180-day deadline, the Revenue & Taxation Division may retroactively reclassify the entity as resident and assess all applicable municipal taxes, MISSA/health-fund contributions, customs duties, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (the banking regulator; the country has no central bank and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands has adopted the U.S. dollar as national legal tender. Both current account and capital account transactions are fully convertible with no foreign exchange controls. Profit remittance via dividends, interest, or license fees to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to corporate law solvency tests and AML/CFT verification. No encumbrances such as surrender or allocation requirements exist. The effective hurdle is correspondent banking due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Because the U.S. dollar is legal tender, export proceeds are not required to be surrendered or converted. There is no mandated timeline or ratio for keeping export receipts in local currency; proceeds may be held directly in USD demand or escrow accounts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low–Medium. The RMI lacks a local EMI/digital bank licensing framework; offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Revolut may facilitate cross-border TT wires in USD, but they are not licensed as banks in RMI and cannot offer escrow or LC services. Legal constraints include the need to route through correspondent banks that may classify RMI-registered corporations as higher risk, and the absence of a formal passporting arrangement. An operational account may be opened remotely with select EMIs, but capital escrow and documentary collections should remain with a licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted only with enhanced due diligence. In practice, tier-1 domestic banks require at least one director or an authorized signatory to attend a physical onboarding interview at the branch; the remaining directors may be onboarded via notarized certified copies, video-conference identification, and validated passports. Remote opening with fintech EMIs generally does not require physical presence, but requires apostilled corporate documents and independent business references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share register, trust deed or control chain documentation, certificate of good standing, and sworn declarations for each ultimate beneficial owner.
Audited financial statements, bank reference from the investor's home bank, board resolution authorizing the capital contribution, and underlying commercial contracts or grant awards.
OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening reports, passport copies, utility statements, PEP declaration form, and explanatory letter for any negative media hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-device sector red flags (false invoicing or product misclassification)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO 13485 certificate, product test certificates, IVD registration documentation, bills of lading, and a detailed business activity narrative reflecting the automated point-of-care IVD manufacturing and microfluidic cartridge production.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inject capital by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank directly to the RMI BC's USD operational or escrow account at the selected tier-1 bank, quoting ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI or EUCP for equity injection. Include the company name, account number, and a unique reference. The receiving bank will verify the remitter's KYC, perform sanctions screening, and may request a board resolution authorizing the capital increase together with a share subscription agreement. No exchange-control approval is required, but wires above USD 500,000 may trigger enhanced due diligence and a request for source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct TT wire payments to suppliers and service providers, and irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP600 for major raw-material import and IVD equipment export transactions. The collecting or advising bank should be a corresponding bank with a USD clearing relationship, for example via Chase, Citi, or Bank of America Merrill Lynch. For LC settlements, ensure compliance with Incoterms, and submit full invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, inspection certificates, and commercial contract excerpts. Outbound wire purpose codes should reflect trade services or receivables financing, subject to the correspondent bank's classification, and supporting documents must be retained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards on restricted or exotic currencies (e.g., USD/INR NDF)
Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR, GBP, or JPY
FX options (calls and puts) for trade and investment exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Corporation (Form AR-1) and Annual Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation; no statutory grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of US$200 per report; if delinquent for two consecutive years, the Registrar may administratively dissolve the corporation without further notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Confirmation (submitted as part of the Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations (through licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual anniversary deadline; agent consent is required at the time of filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent may lead to revocation of the right to transact business and administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Data Verification and Record Update (AML/CFT annual KYC refresh)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (retained as the AML/CFT compliance point); no onshore public UBO registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation (contractual requirement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent may withdraw from representation; the Registrar may dissolve the company for discontinuance of agent services

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-resident domestic corporation that does not have shares listed on a recognized exchange. The Registrar may direct an independent audit if the corporation manages assets in the Marshall Islands or if the public interest so requires.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, with US GAAP also accepted as an equivalent accounting framework for consolidation or reporting to third-party lenders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands does not maintain a public UBO registry. A non-resident corporation must verify and update beneficial ownership data annually through its registered agent under applicable AML/CFT Rules. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members; no annual shareholding declaration is due to the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Agent and Registered Office Record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 850 – 1,500 per annum (includes compliance and corporate secretary support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 9,000 if an audit is requested by a lender or the Registrar; not normally incurred

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (non-resident Business Corporation deriving no income from sources within the Marshall Islands; RMI Income Tax Act applies only to territorial-source income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption from Marshall Islands corporate income tax on foreign-source income; no capital gains tax, no branch remittance tax, no stamp duty on share transfers, no VAT/GST; fully tax-exempt status available to non-resident domestic corporations engaged exclusively in foreign trade and investment, including the manufacture and global distribution of automated point-of-care IVD systems and microfluidic cartridges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Annual Renewal and Tax Status Declaration (Form AR-NDC-2025); filed through the RMI Registrar of Corporations' Online Business Portal (https://www.registrar.gov.mh). For effective tax-exempt maintenance, the BC must file the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Annual Declaration (Schedule A) in the same electronic submission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, regardless of cancellation of profit or lack of activity
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 March following the close of the calendar year; corporations electing a non-calendar fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June) must file within three months of the fiscal year-end; extension of up to 30 days may be granted through the resident agent before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed Resident Agent – name, physical office address in Majuro/Ebeye, and contact email.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the resident agent details exactly as appointed; a non-resident BC is not permitted to act as its own registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Office Address – the official service-of-process address within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This may be the resident agent's office; the box must not be left blank and no P.O. Box addresses are allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Declaration – certification that no gross income was derived from RMI sources during the tax year and that all business activities were conducted outside the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'NON-RESIDENT BC' and attach a schedule describing the IVD manufacturing, distribution, and royalty income streams. The schedule should indicate no RMI customers, no RMI permanent establishment, and no local payroll.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized Capital and Issued Share Capital – amount in USD and class of shares / number of issued and outstanding shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: There is no minimum capital requirement; state 'USD 1,000 authorized, 1 share issued using par value USD 1.00' if no capital has been injected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and Officers – full name, nationality, residential address, and date of appointment of each director/officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: At least one director is required under the Business Corporations Act; the director may be a natural person resident outside the RMI or a foreign corporate director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal Business Activity (NAICS 334516 / ISIC 3250) – description of the commercial model.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Specify 'Manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers for automated point-of-care diagnostics; global sales through foreign distributors; no in-country RMI operations.'

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial Summary – total assets, gross revenue, and net income for the period, prepared on a cash or accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The financial summary may be certified by the directors and kept in the registered file; it is not required to be audited for a non-resident BC, but a copy must be available to the RMI Registrar upon written demand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Optional Tax Exemption / Certificate of Non-Residence request – used for foreign bank account opening and inbound tax relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check the box, specify the jurisdiction (e.g., United States, Taiwan, Germany), and provide the legal entity identifier (LEI) if requested; the Registrar will issue the certificate within 5 business days.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual renewal and non-resident status declaration by the deadline triggers a late penalty of USD 500 and a daily surcharge of USD 50 up to a maximum USD 10,000; if the default continues beyond 90 days, the Registrar may strike the BC from the register and add a reinstatement fee of USD 1,000. Knowingly false declarations are referred to the RMI Criminal Investigation Division and can lead to loss of tax-exempt status and a fine of up to USD 25,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – the Marshall Islands does not impose corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, or branch remittance tax on dividend distributions made by a non-resident BC to its shareholders, regardless of the shareholder's residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI is not a party to any comprehensive income tax treaty (only Tax Information Exchange Agreements and limited bilateral agreements are in force). Therefore, treaty relief is generally unavailable to a non-resident BC. For profit repatriation to a parent in a high-tax jurisdiction, the shareholder must (i) obtain a Marshall Islands Certificate of Tax Exemption / Non-Residence from the Registrar, (ii) submit the certificate together with Form W-8BEN-E (for US withholding) or the parent-jurisdiction's beneficial ownership declaration, and (iii) rely on the shareholder's home-country treaty network or unilateral foreign-tax-credit rules. No RMI clearance, tax residence certificate, or advance ruling is required for the BC's own distribution, but the resident agent should keep a copy of the distribution resolution to evidence the exempt character of the dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate: 0% for patent royalties, licence fees, know-how payments, and bare debt interest when paid by the non-resident BC to foreign counterparties without an RMI source nexus; no treaty rate is applicable because no double tax agreement has been ratified. Where the intellectual property constituting the microfluidic/immunoassay technology is licensed to a foreign operating subsidiary, license agreements should be signed outside the RMI and consideration settled by wire transfer to the BC's account outside the RMI to avoid any accidental RMI-source characterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 (best-practice/voluntary intercompany transaction threshold; the RMI does not impose any statutory local file/master file obligation, but multinational groups using the RMI BC should document related-party transactions exceeding USD 1,000,000 per annum to satisfy the tax administration of the ultimate parent jurisdiction in an OECD-aligned manner).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not statutorily enacted as standalone Economic Substance Regulations in the RMI. However, the RMI is under EU Code of Conduct Group and OECD BEPS Action 5 monitoring for non-resident corporate regimes. The non-resident exemption is available only if the entity (i) does not derive RMI-source income, (ii) maintains a resident agent and registered office, (iii) keeps contemporaneous records evidencing foreign management, and (iv) is not used as a shell to facilitate aggressive tax avoidance. For the automated point-of-care IVD group, substance to document includes: board minutes held in the parent company's jurisdiction, executed intercompany manufacturing/royalty contracts, inventory title transfer outside the RMI, functional/asset/risk analysis of the RMI entity, and a CFC/tax-residence analysis prepared by the group controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false non-resident declarations while selling IVD cartridges/analyzers to RMI clinics through a local agent, or failing to disclose service/freight income generated inside RMI territorial waters.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to USD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years under the RMI Criminal Code; the tax administration may retroactively assess territorial-source tax at 3%, add interest at 12% per annum, and impose fraud penalties of up to 100% of the underreported amount; the Registrar may revoke the BC's certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and interest; upon conviction, directors face a travel ban from the RMI, confiscation of assets, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the RMI BC purely as a paper entity: no foreign manufacturing capacity, no transfer-pricing analysis, no physical office of the parent group, and no actual decision-making on the IP, used to drain intangible profits from the IVD group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: No direct RMI ESR penalty currently exists; the practical sanction is administrative strike-off by the Registrar after 90 days of non-compliance with annual renewal, and foreign tax authorities may apply CFC/transfer-pricing recharacterisation, deny treaty benefits, impose withholding on deemed royalties, and assess penalties of 20%-40% of underpaid tax in the parent jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under RMI corporate law, veil-piercing is permitted when the corporation is a mere instrumentality; directors may be liable for the group's tax restatement, equitable compensation, and legal costs; a foreign court may issue a worldwide asset freeze order against the directors personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving invoiced payments from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions using SWIFT/telegraphic transfers, back-to-back payments through nominee distribution companies, or deliberately misdescribing wire references (e.g., 'consulting fees' instead of IVD product payment) to circumvent bank transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2002 (as amended) is punishable by fines on the BC of up to USD 1,000,000, forfeiture of the sums involved, and suspension/termination of the resident agent's license; the bank's own compliance sanctions may include account closure and a USD 250,000 regulatory penalty per suspicious transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and compliance officers can be criminally fined USD 250,000 and imprisoned for up to 15 years; the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit can request travel bans and asset freezing through mutual legal assistance, and directors may be barred from holding office in any RMI-licensed registered agent or financial institution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Statement & Perjury Before the Registrar
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting an annual renewal that conceals a disqualifying event (e.g., an adverse AML conviction of a shareholder, a share transfer without board consent, or assignment of the IVD patent to a related party without updating Box 7).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A false official statement is a misdemeanor under Title 23 of the RMI Revised Code, carrying a fine of up to USD 20,000 and up to 3 years' imprisonment; the Registrar may disqualify the resident agent and impose an additional regulatory fine of USD 10,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who certified the false statement is personally liable for the fine and restitution of the registration fee; the Registrar may issue a director disqualification order for up to 5 years, preventing service as a director of any RMI corporation or LLC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Repatriation / Dividend Stripping with Abusive Related-Party Terms
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC's 0% withholding regime to strip IVD operating profits through excessive royalties and interest on shareholder loans without arm's-length rates, excessive leverage (thin capitalisation), or back-to-back licensing arrangements that have no commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Within the RMI, if the Income Tax Act is triggered by local-source character of the royalty, a 3% gross-basis tax may be assessed with a 10% monthly late-payment penalty (capped at 50%) and 12% annual interest; outside the RMI, the operating subsidiary's tax authority may impose withholding deficiency assessments and accuracy-related penalties of 20%-40%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving the abusive intercompany prices can be held personally liable in the parent jurisdiction as shadow directors under civil tax recovery statutes; RMI courts may pierce the veil to reach the BC's assets held in trust and enforce judgments against the directors' direct and indirect shareholding interests.
